howto.dashboard.what: Shows whether the assistant is healthy and how people are using it.
howto.dashboard.s1: Look at the status strip at the top. CRM, database and model should all be green.
howto.dashboard.s2: Read the numbers below: how many questions were asked, how many failed, how long answers take.
howto.dashboard.s3: Pick a time range to compare today with last week.
howto.dashboard.r2v: Open Logs and look at the newest errors
howto.dashboard.tip: Red means something is down. Start with the red item.
howto.logs.what: The technical diary of the service. Open it when something does not work.
howto.logs.s1: Choose how far back to look (hours).
howto.logs.s2: Choose a level. Warning and Error are the ones that matter.
howto.logs.s3: Type a word to search, then read the newest lines.
howto.logs.r3v: The newest line tells what failed
howto.logs.tip: Only warnings and errors are kept. Question texts and customer data are never written here.
howto.users.what: Decides who can open this admin panel and what they can do in it.
howto.users.s1: Click Add user and type their Windows account, like DOMAIN\name.
howto.users.s2: Tick the roles they should have.
howto.users.s3: To block someone without deleting them, deactivate them.
howto.users.r3v: Ayse can read the audit trail but cannot change settings
howto.users.tip: Someone who is not listed (and not in a mapped group) cannot open this panel. People who only use the chat are not managed here.
howto.groups.what: Gives a role to everyone in a Windows (AD) group, so you do not add people one by one.
howto.groups.s2: Type the group as DOMAIN\Group, or pick one of your own groups from the list.
howto.groups.s3: Choose the roles every member of that group gets.
howto.groups.r3v: Everyone in that group gets Auditor
howto.groups.tip: Mapping a very large group (like Domain Users) to a powerful role asks for confirmation. Think before you confirm.
howto.roles.what: A role is a named set of permissions, like “Auditor” or “Support”. You give roles to users.
howto.roles.s1: Click New role and give it a name.
howto.roles.s2: Tick what this role may do.
howto.roles.s3: Save, then give the role to people on the Users page.
howto.roles.r2v: See the dashboard and the logs
howto.roles.r3v: Support staff can look, but cannot change anything
howto.roles.tip: The Administrator role is built in and cannot be changed or deleted.
howto.audit.what: A permanent record of who changed what in this panel.
howto.audit.s1: Read the list: time, person, what they did.
howto.audit.s2: Use the filters to find one person, one kind of change or one day.
howto.audit.s3: Need it as a file for an auditor? Use Export.
howto.audit.r2v: Ahmet turned off the Model table at 14:02
howto.audit.tip: It records changes, not questions. Entries cannot be edited or deleted here.
howto.access-log.what: Shows which CRM data was read for each question: who, when, which tables and how many rows. Never the question text or the values.
howto.access-log.s1: Look at the list, newest first.
howto.access-log.s2: Filter by person, table, source or result.
howto.access-log.s3: Check the row count to see how much data one question touched.
howto.access-log.tip: Opening this page is itself recorded in the audit trail. Entries cannot be edited here.
howto.question-view.what: Lets an authorized admin read the questions one user asked, for an audit.
howto.question-view.s2: Read the questions that are shown.
howto.question-view.r2v: The questions Ayse asked since the feature was turned on
howto.question-view.tip: Switched off by default. It only shows questions asked after it was turned on, users see a notice in the chat, and every view is recorded in the audit trail.
howto.data-access.what: Chooses which CRM tables and fields the assistant may use. Anything you close stays invisible to it, whatever the user’s own CRM rights are.
howto.data-access.s1: Find a table. Use the search and the Open / Closed / All buttons.
howto.data-access.s3: Click a row to see its fields and close the sensitive ones.
howto.data-access.s4: Use Check access to test that the table can really be read.
howto.data-access.r3v: Nobody can ask for birthdays, even if their CRM rights allow it
howto.data-access.tip: Fields like ID numbers are closed automatically. Review that list. A table you open also needs read rights for the service account in CRM.
howto.quality.what: A list of test questions with their correct answers. Run it after any change to see whether the assistant still answers correctly.
howto.quality.s1: On the Generate tab, create test questions from your CRM tables.
howto.quality.s2: On the Cases tab, approve the good ones.
howto.quality.s3: On the Run tab, start a check and wait for the report.
howto.quality.s4: Look at the failed cases and find out why.
howto.quality.r3v: If the assistant answers differently, the case shows up as failed
howto.quality.tip: Approve only cases whose question you understand. Only approved cases count in the score.
howto.feedback.what: Shows how users rated answers, and the questions they chose to share with you as examples of what went wrong.
howto.feedback.s1: The dashboard shows how many thumbs up and down answers got, and why.
howto.feedback.s2: This page lists the questions users chose to share. Users only share when they tick the box, and no name is shown.
howto.feedback.s3: Copy a useful one into your acceptance set, then delete it from here.
howto.feedback.r3v: Show accounts with their phone numbers
howto.feedback.tip: Nothing is sent to anyone automatically. Shared questions stay on your server until you delete them.
howto.export.what: Downloads records (audit trail, access log, usage, feedback) as a file you can give to an auditor.
howto.export.s2: Choose the format (CSV opens in Excel) and the dates.
howto.export.s3: Click Export. The file downloads to your computer.
howto.export.s4: To prove the file was not changed, compare its fingerprint as shown on the page.
howto.export.tip: Every export is recorded in the audit trail. Big date ranges can take a while.
howto.design.what: Describe a new table or field you need. The assistant checks what already exists and writes a design document. It creates nothing in CRM.
howto.design.s1: Write what you need in your own words.
howto.design.s2: Optionally add a prefix for new names (like “new”).
howto.design.s3: Click Start design and wait a few minutes. You can leave the page.
howto.design.s4: Open the result or download it as Word, Markdown or JSON.
howto.design.r1v: We need to track vehicle service appointments
howto.design.r2v: A document: reuse the Vehicle table, add an Appointment table with these fields
howto.design.tip: Do not write personal data. Your CRM administrator builds the design by hand from the document.
howto.settings.what: Switches and numbers that control the assistant: limits, features and how long things are kept. Changes apply without restarting.
howto.settings.s1: Pick a group on the left, or search for a setting.
howto.settings.s2: Read the explanation under the name.
howto.settings.s3: Change the value and save it. “Reset” returns the default.
howto.settings.r2v: Chat shows a pause message until you switch it back on
howto.settings.tip: A setting you changed is marked, so you can see what differs from the default. Be careful with limits: too low and users get blocked.
howto.identity.what: Shows how the system sees you: your Windows account, your groups and the roles they give you.
howto.identity.s1: Read your account name at the top.
howto.identity.s2: Check your groups and the roles they map to.
howto.identity.s3: Use it when someone says “I cannot open page X”: compare their groups and roles here.
howto.identity.r3v: Ayse can open the audit trail
howto.identity.tip: Only you see this page about yourself. Nothing here can be changed.
howto.documents.what: Plain-text notes the assistant reads when it answers: a company policy, what a field means, which old field to avoid.
howto.documents.s1: Click Add document. Start from an example or write your own.
howto.documents.s2: Give it a short title and write one topic. Use the words your users use and the real field names.
howto.documents.s3: Save, then type a question under Try a question to check that your document is found.
howto.documents.s4: Make sure the knowledge setting is on (Settings), otherwise the assistant does not read documents.
howto.documents.r2v:
Support is available Monday to Friday, 09:00-18:00. Cases opened outside these hours are handled the next business day.
CRM: incident
howto.documents.r3v: Asked “show cases opened outside support hours”, the assistant finds this note and builds the query from it
howto.documents.tip: One topic per document, and no personal data. An exact rule like “big customer = more than 1000 employees”? Use the business glossary instead.
howto.glossary.what: Teaches the assistant your company’s own words. When someone asks about “big companies”, the glossary says which filter that means.
howto.glossary.s1: Click Add term and type the word the way people say it, in every language you use (big company, büyük firma).
howto.glossary.s2: Pick Filter for an exact condition that is always applied, or Alias for a hint about which table or field a word means.
howto.glossary.s3: Choose the table, field, operator and value.
howto.glossary.s4: Click Try to see how many records match before you save.
howto.glossary.s5: Save. The next question that uses the word applies it.
howto.glossary.r3v: Number of employees is greater than 1000
howto.glossary.r4v: Asked “show opportunities of big companies”, the system adds the filter itself and the answer says “big company (glossary): …”
howto.glossary.tip: Only an explanation, not an exact rule? Write it on the Documents page instead. Terms that need counting or related records (for example “loyal customer = 3 or more orders”) are not supported here yet.
